header.name: Explainable AI
header.description: This course provides an introduction to Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), focusing on methods that enhance the interpretability and transparency of AI systems. Both traditional (non-symbolic) and modern (symbolic) XAI techniques will be explored, with special attention to leveraging ontologies and knowledge graphs for explainability. Key topics include model-agnostic and model-specific approaches, evaluation metrics for explanations, and ethical considerations in deploying AI systems.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students can assess and compare different XAI methods (e.g., model-agnostic vs. model-specific) based on metrics like interpretability, fidelity, and robustness.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students can demonstrate the ability to apply and evaluate non-symbolic XAI techniques such as LIME and SHAP on machine learning models.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students can create AI systems that integrate ontologies or knowledge graphs with machine learning models, demonstrating improved transparency and reasoning.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students can design and implement an XAI solution for a domain-specific problem (e.g., healthcare diagnostics, fraud detection) and justify their approach.

lecture_topics: Types of explainability and XAI methods
introduction to ontologies and knowledge graphs
Case studies from different domains and applications (healthcare, finance, recommendation systems etc.)
